newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African vigilante leader surrenders.
newsitem.headline: S.African vigilante leader surrenders.

text.p: A South African Moslem vigilante wanted for organising a violent protest at Cape Town international airport gave himself up to police on Thursday but a second was on the run, police said.

Police had given the two leaders of People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (Pagad) until 3 p.m. (1300 GMT) to report voluntarily on charges arising from an illegal demonstration police broke up with police dogs, tear gas and rubber bullet.
Superintendent John Sterrenberg said Aslam Toefy gave himself up and was put into custody. Sterrenberg said the police would search for the second Pagad leader, Abdus-Salaam Ebrahim.
Pagad on Monday had organised a protest at the Cape Town airport, which the group said was being used to smuggle in drugs.
Police said the demonstration was illegal and fired tear gas and rubber bullets, arresting a total of 24 vigilantes during the demonstration and a later protest outside a police station.
Pagad leapt to prominence in August when members killed the leader of a notorious gang in front of television cameras.

Mandela's government initially showed some sympathy for the group's anti-crime programme but police officers said this week PAGAD's actions put it in the same category as the gangs it claimed to be fighting.
The 24 PAGAD members arrested on Monday are due to appear in court on Friday to apply for bail.
